ASANAS.name: Tadasana
ASANAS.description: The foundational standing posture in yoga that promotes balance, spinal alignment, and body awareness.
benefits: Improves posture and spinal alignment
Strengthens thighs, knees, and ankles
Firms abdomen and buttocks
Reduces flat feet issues
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe headache or insomnia
Use support if experiencing low blood pressure or lightheadedness
steps: Stand with your big toes touching, heels slightly apart.
Distribute your weight evenly across the four corners of your feet.
Engage your thigh muscles and draw your belly inward and upward.
Roll your shoulders back and down, allowing your arms to rest naturally by your sides with palms facing forward.
Keep your head aligned over your heart, look straight ahead, and breathe slowly.

ASANAS.name: Vrikshasana
ASANAS.description: A balancing pose that replicates the steady, rooted nature of a tree, enhancing focus and equilibrium.
benefits: Establishes physical and mental balance
Strengthens the ligaments and tendons of the feet and ankles
Tones the leg muscles and improves hip mobility
Increases concentration and mental focus
precautions: Avoid if you have acute knee injuries
Be careful in case of high blood pressure (keep hands on hips instead of overhead)
steps: Begin in Tadasana, shifting your weight onto your left foot.
Bend your right knee and place the sole of your right foot on the inner left thigh (avoiding the knee joint).
Press the right foot into the thigh and the thigh into the foot to create resistance.
Bring your hands into prayer position (Anjali Mudra) at your chest or extend them overhead.
Focus your gaze on a steady point (Drishti) in front of you and hold for several deep breaths.

ASANAS.name: Bhujangasana
ASANAS.description: A gentle backward bend that stretches the chest and strengthens the spine, simulating a raised cobra.
benefits: Strengthens the spine and back muscles
Stretches the chest, lungs, shoulders, and abdomen
Stimulates abdominal organs and helps relieve stress/fatigue
Therapeutic for asthma by opening the chest cavity
precautions: Avoid during pregnancy
Not recommended for those with carpal tunnel syndrome or recent abdominal surgery
Avoid in case of acute back injury or hernia
steps: Lie flat on your stomach, forehead resting on the floor, legs extended.
Place your hands under your shoulders, hugging your elbows close to your torso.
Press the tops of your feet and thighs firmly into the mat.
Inhale and lift your chest off the floor, keeping your elbows bent and shoulders relaxed away from your ears.
Keep your gaze slightly forward and down to avoid straining the neck; breathe softly.

ASANAS.name: Vajrasana
ASANAS.description: A kneeling posture that is one of the few yoga poses recommended to perform immediately after a meal to aid digestion.
benefits: Enhances digestive capacity and cures acidity or bloating
Strengthens thighs, calves, and knees
Keeps the spine upright and improves posture
Calms the mind, making it excellent for meditation
precautions: Do not practice if you have severe knee pain, arthritis of knees, or ankle injuries
Avoid if suffering from severe piles or hernia
steps: Kneel on the floor with your big toes touching and heels separated.
Lower your hips so you are sitting on the heels, resting your buttocks in the space between them.
Place your hands on your knees with palms facing downwards.
Keep your spine straight, shoulders relaxed, and gaze forward.
Breathe deeply and focus on the abdominal region.

ASANAS.name: Shavasana
ASANAS.description: A posture of total relaxation, usually practiced at the end of a session to integrate the physical benefits of practice.
benefits: Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and mild depression
Relaxes the entire nervous system and reduces blood pressure
Relieves headache, fatigue, and insomnia
Enhances self-awareness and mindfulness
precautions: If you experience back discomfort, place a bolster or pillow under your knees
steps: Lie flat on your back, legs extended and slightly apart, allowing feet to drop open.
Place your arms slightly away from your body with palms facing up.
Close your eyes and release all muscular tension, starting from your toes up to your head.
Let your breathing become natural, quiet, and effortless.
Maintain a state of quiet awareness, avoiding sleep or wandering thoughts.

ASANAS.name: Setu Bandhasana
ASANAS.description: A rejuvenating backbend that stimulates the thyroid, opens the chest, and strengthens the legs and core.
benefits: Stretches the chest, neck, and spine
Stimulates abdominal organs, lungs, and thyroid gland
Reduces anxiety, fatigue, backache, headache, and insomnia
Improves digestion and provides relief from menopause symptoms
precautions: Avoid if you have neck or shoulder injuries
Avoid during late-stage pregnancy unless supported by a block
steps: Lie on your back, bend your knees, and place your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Position your heels close to your sit bones.
Inhale, press your feet and arms into the floor, and lift your hips toward the ceiling.
Clasp your hands together beneath your pelvis, rolling your shoulders closer together.
Keep your thighs parallel to each other and lift your chest toward your chin.

ASANAS.name: Paschimottanasana
ASANAS.description: A deep forward fold that stretches the entire back of the body, particularly the hamstrings and lower spine.
benefits: Stretches hamstrings, shoulders, spine, and lower back
Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and mild depression
Stimulates the liver, kidneys, ovaries, and uterus
Aids digestion and relieves symptoms of menopause and menstrual discomfort
precautions: Avoid if you have asthma or severe diarrhea
Contraindicated in case of a herniated disc or severe back injury
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you (Dandasana).
Inhale, extend your arms overhead, lengthening your spine.
Exhale and fold forward from your hips, keeping your chest open and spine long.
Reach for your shins, ankles, or feet with your hands.
With each inhale, lengthen the spine slightly; with each exhale, fold deeper, keeping the neck relaxed.

ASANAS.name: Trikonasana
ASANAS.description: A standing pose that stretches and tones the entire body, creating a shape of three interlocking triangles.
benefits: Stretches and strengthens thighs, knees, and ankles
Stretches hips, groins, hamstrings, calves, shoulders, chest, and spine
Stimulates abdominal organs and helps relieve stress
Relieves backache, especially during pregnancy
precautions: Avoid if you have low blood pressure, severe neck problems, or migraine
In case of high blood pressure, look down rather than up at the raised hand
steps: Stand with feet wide apart (about 3-4 feet). Turn your right foot out 90 degrees and left foot in slightly.
Inhale and extend your arms out to the sides, parallel to the floor.
Exhale, reach your torso to the right, bending from the hip joint, not the waist.
Place your right hand on your shin, ankle, or the floor outside your right foot.
Stretch your left arm straight up toward the ceiling, keeping your shoulders stacked, and look up at your thumb.

ASANAS.name: Padmasana
ASANAS.description: The classic meditative posture that locks the body in place, encourages a straight spine, and directs energy flow.
benefits: Calms the brain and redirects energy towards meditation
Stimulates the pelvis, spine, abdomen, and bladder
Stretches the ankles and knees
Helps improve posture and spinal curvature
precautions: Avoid if you have severe ankle or knee injuries
Requires high hip flexibility; do not force the knees into position
steps: Sit on the floor with legs extended. Bend the right knee and cradle it, placing the foot in the crease of the left hip.
Bend the left knee, gently lifting the left foot and crossing it over the folded right leg to place it in the right hip crease.
Keep both knees as close to the floor as possible.
Straighten your spine, place your hands on your knees in Gyan Mudra (thumb and index finger touching).
Close your eyes and breathe deeply.

ASANAS.name: Sukhasana
ASANAS.description: A comfortable cross-legged sitting posture ideal for meditation and breathing exercises.
benefits: Promotes inner calm and mental focus
Stretches the knees and ankles
Opens the hips and strengthens the back muscles
Excellent foundational pose for pranayama
precautions: Use a folded blanket or block under your sit bones if your knees are raised high above your hips
steps: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you.
Cross your shins and slide your feet under the opposite knees.
Rest the outer edges of your feet comfortably on the floor.
Align your head, neck, and spine. Place your hands on your knees with palms up or down.
Relax your shoulders and breathe steadily.

ASANAS.name: Surya Namaskar
ASANAS.description: A comprehensive sequence of 12 fluid postures that warm up the body, balance energy flow, and build strength and flexibility.
benefits: Provides a complete body workout, burning calories and toning muscles
Improves blood circulation and respiration throughout the body
Promotes flexibility in the spine, hamstrings, and shoulders
Balances the hormonal system by stimulating the endocrine glands
precautions: Avoid in case of severe high blood pressure or hernia
Not recommended during menstruation or late-stage pregnancy
Avoid if suffering from severe back ailments or slip disc
steps: Pranamasana (Prayer Pose): Stand at the edge of the mat, palms in prayer.
Hasta Uttanasana (Raised Arms Pose): Inhale, raise arms and bend backward.
Padahastasana (Hand to Foot Pose): Exhale, fold forward and bring hands to feet.
Ashwa Sanchalanasana (Equestrian Pose): Inhale, step the right leg back, chest up.
Dandasana (Plank Pose): Step left leg back, keep body in a straight line.
Ashtanga Namaskara (Salute with Eight Parts): Exhale, lower chest, knees, and chin to floor.
Bhujangasana (Cobra Pose): Inhale, slide forward and arch your back.
Adho Mukha Svanasana (Downward Facing Dog): Exhale, lift hips up, head down.
Ashwa Sanchalanasana (Equestrian Pose): Inhale, step right foot forward between hands.
Padahastasana (Hand to Foot Pose): Exhale, step left foot forward and fold.
Hasta Uttanasana (Raised Arms Pose): Inhale, rise up, stretch arms overhead, bend back.
Pranamasana (Prayer Pose): Exhale, return to standing prayer position.

ASANAS.name: Adho Mukha Svanasana
ASANAS.description: An inversion pose that stretches the entire body, strengthening the shoulders, arms, and legs while calming the mind.
benefits: Stretches the shoulders, hamstrings, calves, and hands
Strengthens the arms and legs
Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and mild depression
Improves digestion and relieves headaches and fatigue
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe carpal tunnel syndrome
Do not practice during late-term pregnancy
steps: Start on your hands and knees, with wrists directly under shoulders and knees under hips.
Spread your fingers wide and press firmly through your palms.
Exhale, tuck your toes, and lift your knees off the floor, reaching your pelvis up toward the ceiling.
Lengthen your spine and push your thighs back. Straighten your legs without locking your knees.
Let your head hang naturally between your arms, looking toward your toes.

ASANAS.name: Balasana
ASANAS.description: A restorative resting pose that gently stretches the hips, thighs, and ankles while relieving stress and tension.
benefits: Gently stretches the hips, thighs, and ankles
Calms the mind and central nervous system
Relieves back and neck pain when practiced with support
precautions: Avoid if suffering from acute knee injuries
Avoid during pregnancy
steps: Kneel on the floor, touch your big toes together, and sit on your heels.
Separate your knees about as wide as your hips.
Exhale and lay your torso down between your thighs.
Lay your hands on the floor alongside your torso, palms up, and release the fronts of your shoulders toward the floor.
Rest your forehead gently on the mat and breathe deeply.

ASANAS.name: Virabhadrasana I
ASANAS.description: A powerful standing posture that stretches the chest and lungs while strengthening the shoulders, arms, and back muscles.
benefits: Strengthens the shoulders, arms, legs, and back muscles
Stretches the chest, lungs, shoulders, and groin
Improves balance and focus
precautions: Avoid if suffering from high blood pressure or heart conditions
Keep the head in a neutral position if experiencing neck injuries
steps: Start in Tadasana. Step your left foot back about 3 to 4 feet.
Turn your left foot inward 45 to 60 degrees. Align your right heel with your left heel.
Exhale and bend your right knee over the right ankle so that the shin is perpendicular to the floor.
Reach your arms up overhead, parallel to each other, palms facing in.
Press your back heel firmly into the floor and reach up through your fingers.

ASANAS.name: Virabhadrasana II
ASANAS.description: A foundational standing pose that improves stamina, tones abdominal muscles, and increases hip flexibility.
benefits: Strengthens and stretches the legs and ankles
Stretches the groin, chest, and shoulders
Stimulates abdominal organs and increases stamina
Relieves backaches and therapeutic for flat feet
precautions: Avoid in cases of recent hip or knee replacements
Keep head looking forward if neck pain is present
steps: Stand in Tadasana. Step your left foot back 3 to 4 feet.
Turn your left foot out 90 degrees and align your right heel with the arch of your left foot.
Raise your arms parallel to the floor, extending them actively out to the sides.
Exhale and bend your right knee over your right ankle, keeping the thigh parallel to the floor.
Turn your head to the right and look out over your right fingers.

ASANAS.name: Virabhadrasana III
ASANAS.description: A challenging balance posture that strengthens the entire back leg, ankle, and core stabilizers.
benefits: Strengthens the ankles, legs, shoulders, and back muscles
Tones the abdomen and improves posture
Develops physical coordination, balance, and deep focus
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe balance disorders or low blood pressure
Practice near a wall for safety if needed
steps: Start in Warrior I with your right foot forward.
Lean your torso forward and shift your weight entirely onto your right foot.
Slowly lift your left leg up behind you as you straighten your right leg.
Lower your torso until it is parallel to the floor, extending your arms straight forward.
Keep your gaze focused on a fixed point on the floor.

ASANAS.name: Utkatasana
ASANAS.description: A heating standing pose that stimulates the heart, diaphragm, and abdominal organs while building lower-body strength.
benefits: Strengthens the ankles, calves, thighs, and spine
Stretches the shoulders and chest
Stimulates the abdominal organs, heart, and diaphragm
Reduces flat feet symptoms
precautions: Avoid if suffering from chronic headaches or insomnia
Do not practice if experiencing acute knee pain
steps: Stand straight in Tadasana with feet slightly apart or touching.
Inhale and raise your arms overhead, perpendicular to the floor.
Exhale and bend your knees, shifting your hips back and down as if sitting in an imaginary chair.
Keep your chest lifted and your back straight, drawing your lower belly in.
Hold the posture while breathing deeply through the nose.

ASANAS.name: Marjaryasana
ASANAS.description: A gentle spinal movement that stretches the back torso and neck, releasing tension in the spine.
benefits: Stretches the back torso, neck, and spine
Gently stimulates the kidneys and adrenal glands
Relieves neck and shoulder tension
precautions: If experiencing neck injuries, keep the head in alignment with the torso
steps: Start on hands and knees in a tabletop position.
Exhale, pull your belly button toward your spine, and round your back toward the ceiling.
Release your head toward the floor, tucking your chin slightly toward your chest.
Press firmly through your hands to expand the space between your shoulder blades.

ASANAS.name: Bitilasana
ASANAS.description: A gentle backbend that stretches the front torso and neck, usually paired with Cat Pose to warm up the spine.
benefits: Stretches the front torso, chest, and neck
Warms up the spine and coordinates breath with movement
Calms the mind and relieves stress
precautions: If experiencing lower back sensitivity, perform the backbend gently
steps: Start on hands and knees in a tabletop position.
Inhale, drop your belly down toward the floor, and lift your chest and hips toward the ceiling.
Draw your shoulders back and look gently upward.
Keep your core engaged to protect the lower back.

ASANAS.name: Baddha Konasana
ASANAS.description: A seated hip opener that stretches the inner thighs and groin, stimulating abdominal and reproductive organs.
benefits: Stretches the inner thighs, groins, and knees
Stimulates abdominal organs, ovaries, prostate gland, and kidneys
Improves blood circulation in the pelvis
Relieves mild depression, anxiety, and fatigue
precautions: If suffering from knee injuries, place blocks under the outer thighs for support
steps: Sit with your legs straight in front of you.
Exhale, bend your knees, pull your heels toward your pelvis, and drop your knees out to the sides, pressing the soles of your feet together.
Hold your feet or ankles. Keep your spine long and chest open.
Gently press the outer thighs down toward the floor without forcing.

ASANAS.name: Gomukhasana
ASANAS.description: A deep shoulder and hip opener that releases tension in the upper back and stimulates the kidneys.
benefits: Deeply stretches the shoulders, armpits, triceps, and chest
Opens the hips and stretches the outer thighs
Tones the arms and helps treat sciatica
precautions: If shoulders are tight, use a strap or towel to connect the hands behind the back
steps: Sit in a comfortable cross-legged position, then stack your right knee directly on top of your left knee.
Inhale and reach your right arm up, bend your elbow, and place your right hand on your upper back.
Reach your left arm down and back, bend the elbow, and slide your left hand up to clasp your right fingers.
Keep your chest lifted and head straight, breathing deeply.

ASANAS.name: Shalabhasana
ASANAS.description: A prone backbend that strengthens the entire back body, shoulders, and glutes, preparing for deeper backbends.
benefits: Strengthens the muscles of the spine, buttocks, and back of the arms
Stretches the shoulders, chest, belly, and thighs
Improves posture and stimulates abdominal organs
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe neck or lower back injuries
Do not practice during pregnancy
steps: Lie on your belly with your arms at your sides, palms up, and forehead resting on the floor.
Inhale, and lift your head, chest, arms, and legs off the floor.
Reach back through your legs and feet, keeping your thighs engaged.
Keep your gaze forward or slightly down to avoid straining the back of your neck.

ASANAS.name: Dhanurasana
ASANAS.description: An intense backbend that opens the chest and stretches the front body while massaging the abdominal organs.
benefits: Stretches the entire front of the body, ankles, thighs, and groins
Deeply opens the chest and shoulders
Massages the liver, pancreas, and kidneys, improving digestion
precautions: Avoid if suffering from high blood pressure, hernia, or ulcers
Do not practice if experiencing migraine headaches
steps: Lie on your belly with your arms at your sides.
Bend your knees and bring your heels close to your buttocks.
Reach back with your hands and clasp your ankles.
Inhale, lift your heels away from your buttocks and lift your thighs off the floor. This will pull your chest off the mat.
Look forward and breathe evenly.

ASANAS.name: Ustrasana
ASANAS.description: A deep backward bending posture that stretches the entire anterior chain and stimulates the thyroid gland.
benefits: Stretches the chest, abdomen, quadriceps, and psoas muscles
Improves spinal flexibility and posture
Stimulates the thyroid and endocrine glands
precautions: Avoid if suffering from high or low blood pressure
Do not practice if experiencing severe neck injuries
steps: Kneel on the floor with your knees hip-width apart.
Press your shins and the tops of your feet firmly into the floor.
Place your hands on your lower back, fingers pointing down.
Inhale, lift your chest, and slowly lean back, reaching your hands to clasp your heels.
Keep your hips aligned over your knees and let your head drop back gently if safe for your neck.

ASANAS.name: Matsyasana
ASANAS.description: A supine backbend that opens the chest, lungs, and throat, relieving tension in the neck and shoulders.
benefits: Stretches the deep hip flexors and intercostal muscles
Relieves tension in the neck, throat, and shoulders
Expands respiratory capacity, assisting in asthma relief
Tones the pituitary, adrenal, and pineal glands
precautions: Avoid if suffering from high blood pressure, insomnia, or migraines
steps: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent, feet on the floor.
Slide your hands, palms down, under your buttocks.
Inhale, press your elbows and forearms firmly into the floor, and lift your upper torso and head off the mat.
Arch your back and gently rest the crown of your head on the floor.
Keep the weight of your body in your forearms and elbows, not on your head.

ASANAS.name: Halasana
ASANAS.description: An inversion that stretches the back muscles, spine, and neck, calming the nervous system and improving thyroid health.
benefits: Stretches the back muscles and entire spine
Massages internal organs, aiding digestion and constipation
Stimulates the thyroid gland and helps manage metabolism
precautions: Avoid if suffering from cervical spine issues or slipped discs
Do not practice during menstruation or pregnancy
steps: Lie on your back, arms by your sides. Lift your legs straight up to 90 degrees.
Press your arms into the floor and lift your hips up, rolling your spine off the floor.
Bring your legs overhead until your toes touch the floor behind your head.
Support your lower back with your hands or interlace your fingers on the floor.
Keep your neck straight; do not turn your head from side to side.

ASANAS.name: Sarvangasana
ASANAS.description: Considered the 'Queen of Asanas', this inversion stimulates the thyroid gland, relieves varicose veins, and calms the mind.
benefits: Directly stimulates the thyroid and parathyroid glands
Improves blood circulation to the brain and upper body
Relieves pressure in the lower body, aiding varicose veins
Calms the nervous system and reduces anxiety
precautions: Do not practice if suffering from high blood pressure, glaucoma, or neck injuries
Contraindicated during menstruation
steps: Lie on your back. Bend your knees, then press your arms down and lift your hips.
Bend your elbows and place your hands on your lower back for support.
Walk your hands up your back toward your shoulders and extend your legs straight up.
Align your torso and legs as vertically as possible, resting your weight on your shoulders.
Keep your gaze focused on your big toes.

ASANAS.name: Sirsasana
ASANAS.description: Considered the 'King of Asanas', this powerful inversion redirects oxygenated blood to the brain, improving focus, memory, and pituitary health.
benefits: Increases blood flow to the brain, improving cognitive function
Strengthens the shoulders, neck, arms, and core stabilizers
Stimulates the pituitary and pineal glands
Improves digestion and helps relieve stress and insomnia
precautions: Avoid if suffering from high blood pressure, glaucoma, or neck injuries
Contraindicated during pregnancy and menstruation
steps: Kneel on the floor, interlace your fingers, and place your forearms on the mat.
Place the crown of your head on the floor, cradled by your interlaced hands.
Tuck your toes, lift your knees, and walk your feet toward your elbows.
Engage your core, lift one leg at a time or both together, extending them vertically.
Keep the majority of the weight supported by your forearms, keeping neck compressed minimally.

ASANAS.name: Bakasana
ASANAS.description: An arm balance that strengthens the wrists, arms, and shoulders while demanding deep core stabilization and mental focus.
benefits: Strengthens the arms, wrists, and shoulders
Engages and tones the abdominal core muscles
Stretches the upper back and increases balance and concentration
precautions: Avoid if suffering from carpal tunnel syndrome or wrist injuries
Contraindicated during pregnancy
steps: Squat down and place your hands flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Spread your fingers wide. Lift your hips high and place your knees on the backs of your upper arms, near the armpits.
Lean forward, shifting your weight into your hands.
Engage your core and lift one foot, then the other, off the floor.
Bring your heels up toward your buttocks and look slightly forward.

ASANAS.name: Ardha Matsyendrasana
ASANAS.englishName: Half Lord of the Fishes Pose
ASANAS.description: A seated spinal twist that stretches the spine, hips, and chest, stimulating digestion and metabolic rate.
benefits: Tones and stretches the spine, improving flexibility
Stimulates liver, kidneys, and pancreas, beneficial for diabetes
Opens the chest, shoulders, and hips
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe back or spine injuries, slipped discs, or recent abdominal surgery
steps: Sit on the floor with legs extended forward.
Bend your left knee and slide the left foot under your right thigh, placing it near the outer right hip.
Step your right foot over your left knee and place it flat on the floor.
Inhale, reach your left arm up, then exhale and hook your left elbow on the outside of your right knee.
Place your right hand on the floor behind you and twist your torso gently to the right.

ASANAS.name: Malasana
ASANAS.description: A deep yogic squat that stretches the ankles, groin, and back torso while improving digestive functions.
benefits: Stretches the ankles, groins, and back torso
Tones the abdominal muscles and improves digestion
Provides deep emotional grounding and anxiety relief
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe knee or hip pain
steps: Stand with your feet slightly wider than hip-width, toes turned slightly out.
Bend your knees and lower your hips down into a deep squat.
Bring your palms together in prayer position (Anjali Mudra) at your chest.
Press your elbows against your inner knees to gently open the hips.
Lengthen your spine and drop your shoulders away from your ears.

ASANAS.name: Janu Sirsasana
ASANAS.description: A seated forward bend that stretches the hamstrings and spine, massaging the kidneys and liver.
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings, spine, and groin
Massages the liver, spleen, and kidneys
Calms the brain and helps relieve mild anxiety and depression
precautions: Avoid if suffering from chronic asthma or slipped discs
Keep the knee supported if experiencing joint pain
steps: Sit with your legs straight in front of you.
Bend your left knee and place the sole of your left foot against your inner right thigh.
Inhale, reach your arms up, and lengthen your spine.
Exhale, hinge from your hips, and fold forward over your straight right leg.
Hold your foot, ankle, or shin, keeping your neck relaxed.

ASANAS.name: Uttanasana
ASANAS.description: A standing forward fold that intensely stretches the hamstrings, calves, and back, reducing anxiety and stress.
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings, calves, and hips
Strengthens the knees and thighs
Calms the nervous system and relieves stress
precautions: Bend the knees slightly if suffering from lower back sensitivity
Avoid if experiencing severe vertigo
steps: Stand straight in Tadasana, hands on your hips.
Exhale and fold forward from your hip joints, not from your waist.
Extend your torso down and place your hands on the floor beside your feet, or hold your ankles.
Let the crown of your head hang down and relax your neck.
Breathe deeply, letting gravity stretch your spine.

ASANAS.name: Garudasana
ASANAS.description: A standing balance pose that opens the back shoulders, hips, and ankles, requiring deep mental focus.
benefits: Strengthens and stretches the ankles and calves
Stretches the thighs, hips, shoulders, and upper back
Improves balance, visual focus, and coordination
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe knee or ankle injuries
steps: Stand in Tadasana. Bend your knees slightly.
Lift your left leg, and wrap your left thigh over your right thigh. Hook your left foot behind your right calf.
Stretch your arms straight forward. Cross your left arm under your right arm.
Bend your elbows, wrap your forearms, and press your palms together.
Balance on your right foot and sit your hips down as if in Chair Pose.

ASANAS.name: Natarajasana
ASANAS.description: A beautiful standing backbend and balance pose that opens the shoulders and chest while building balance.
benefits: Strengthens the legs, ankles, and core stabilizers
Stretches the shoulders, chest, thighs, and abdomen
Improves balance, concentration, and poise
precautions: Avoid in cases of severe balance disorders or knee injuries
Do not strain the lower back; lift the leg gently
steps: Stand in Tadasana. Shift your weight onto your right foot.
Bend your left knee and reach back with your left hand to grasp the inside of your left ankle.
Inhale, reach your right arm straight up overhead.
Exhale, kick your left foot back and up, lifting your thigh parallel to the floor.
Lean your torso forward slightly, keeping your chest open and eyes focused forward.

ASANAS.name: Viparita Karani
ASANAS.description: A restorative inversion that relieves pressure in the lower extremities, calms the nervous system, and reduces leg swelling.
benefits: Relieves tired or cramped legs and feet
Gently stretches the back hamstrings and neck
Facilitates venous drainage, reducing leg swelling and varicose veins
Induces deep parasympathetic calming, reducing stress and anxiety
precautions: Avoid in cases of glaucoma or severe eye conditions due to pressure shifts
Place a bolster or folded blanket under the pelvis for comfort
steps: Sit sideways with your right hip close to a wall.
Exhale, gently swing your legs up onto the wall, and lower your shoulders and head flat onto the floor.
Adjust your body so your sit bones are close to the wall (or resting on a prop).
Let your arms rest comfortably out to the sides, palms up.
Close your eyes and breathe slowly, letting your leg muscles relax.

ASANAS.name: Makarasana
ASANAS.description: A relaxing prone posture that is highly effective for relieving lower back pain and promoting diaphragmatic breathing.
benefits: Relieves lower back pain, tension, and strain
Encourages deep, natural diaphragmatic breathing
Pacifies the nervous system, helpful for insomnia and high blood pressure
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe respiratory distress or in late-term pregnancy
steps: Lie on your stomach on the floor.
Cross your forearms in front of you and rest your forehead or chin on your hands.
Separate your legs wide, with your heels turned inward and toes pointing outward.
Close your eyes and allow your whole body to sink into the floor, focusing on the movement of your breath in your lower back.

ASANAS.name: Pawanmuktasana
ASANAS.description: A supine posture that compresses the abdominal organs, relieving gas, constipation, and lower back tension.
benefits: Massages the abdominal organs, expelling trapped gases and curing constipation
Stretches and decompresses the lumbar spine, relieving lower back pain
Improves blood circulation in the pelvic region
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe hernia, sciatica, or neck injuries
Do not practice after recent abdominal surgery
steps: Lie on your back, legs extended. Exhale, bend both knees, and draw them to your chest.
Clasp your hands or arms over your shins.
Inhale, and as you exhale, lift your head and chest off the floor, bringing your nose or forehead toward your knees.
Hold the position while breathing gently, then release back down.

ASANAS.name: Supta Baddha Konasana
ASANAS.description: A deeply restorative supine pose that opens the hips and groin, cooling the nervous system and easing pelvic tension.
benefits: Opens the hips and groins, relieving pelvic congestion
Stimulates abdominal organs, ovaries, and kidneys
Deeply restorative, reducing stress, anxiety, and premenstrual symptoms
precautions: Support knees with bolsters or blocks if groin or hip joints feel strained
steps: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the floor.
Bring the soles of your feet together and let your knees fall open to the sides.
Rest your arms on the floor, palms facing up, a comfortable distance from your body.
Let gravity open your hips passively while focusing on slow abdominal breathing.

ASANAS.name: Anjaneyasana
ASANAS.description: A deep lunge that stretches the hip flexors, quadriceps, and opens the chest, improving posture and energy.
benefits: Deeply stretches the hip flexors (psoas) and quadriceps
Opens the chest, lungs, and shoulders
Strengthens the knees, ankles, and glutes
precautions: Place a blanket under the back knee if experiencing joint discomfort
Avoid stretching too deeply if suffering from groin strain
steps: Start in Downward-Facing Dog. Step your right foot forward between your hands.
Lower your left knee to the floor and slide it back, keeping top of foot flat on the mat.
Inhale and sweep your arms overhead, lifting your torso.
Shift your hips forward and down, keeping right knee directly over the right ankle.
Reach up through your fingers and look gently upward.

ASANAS.name: Parsvottanasana
ASANAS.description: A deep forward fold over one leg that intensely stretches the hamstrings, calf muscles, and spine, improving balance.
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings, spine, hips, and shoulders
Stimulates abdominal organs, aiding digestion
Improves physical balance and mental focus
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe lower back injuries or high blood pressure
Keep knees slightly bent if hamstrings are extremely tight
steps: Stand in Tadasana. Step your left foot back about 2 to 3 feet.
Turn your left foot out 45 degrees. Turn your hips to face forward.
Inhale, reach your arms up (or clasp them behind your back in reverse prayer).
Exhale, hinge from your hips, and fold forward over your straight right leg.
Rest your hands on your shin, blocks, or the floor, drawing your forehead toward your knee.

ASANAS.name: Ardha Chandrasana
ASANAS.description: A balancing pose that opens the hips and chest, strengthening the ankles and core stabilizers.
benefits: Strengthens the ankles, knees, thighs, and buttocks
Stretches the hamstrings, groin, chest, and shoulders
Improves coordination, balance, and core stability
precautions: Avoid if suffering from migraines, insomnia, or low blood pressure
Practice with a hand on a block for stability
steps: Start in Triangle Pose with your right foot forward.
Bend your right knee slightly and place your right hand on the floor (or a block) 12 inches ahead of your foot.
Shift your weight onto your right foot and lift your left leg parallel to the floor.
Rotate your left hip open, stacking it on top of your right hip.
Extend your left arm straight up toward the ceiling and look toward your left fingers if balanced.

ASANAS.name: Uttana Shishosana
ASANAS.description: A cross between Child's Pose and Downward-Facing Dog that opens the shoulders and upper back, relieving spinal tension.
benefits: Stretches the shoulders and upper back
Opens the chest and thoracic spine
Calms the mind and helps relieve chronic stress and tension
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe shoulder injuries
Place a blanket under the knees for support if needed
steps: Start on hands and knees in a tabletop position.
Walk your hands forward, keeping your hips stacked directly over your knees.
Exhale and lower your chest toward the floor, resting your forehead or chin on the mat.
Reach actively through your arms, keeping your elbows lifted off the mat.

ASANAS.name: Purvottanasana
ASANAS.description: An intense front-body stretch that strengthens the arms, wrists, and legs while opening the chest and shoulders.
benefits: Strengthens the wrists, arms, shoulders, and legs
Stretches the chest, shoulders, and front of the ankles
Tones the core and back extensor muscles
precautions: Avoid in cases of severe carpal tunnel syndrome or neck injuries
steps: Sit in Dandasana (Staff Pose) with hands on the floor behind your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Bend your knees slightly or keep legs straight. Press your hands and feet firmly into the floor.
Inhale, lift your hips high, and extend your chest toward the ceiling.
Straighten your legs, pressing the soles of your feet toward the floor.
Drop your head back gently if your neck feels comfortable.

ASANAS.name: Navasana
ASANAS.description: A core-strengthening pose that stimulates the thyroid and abdominal organs while building balance and willpower.
benefits: Strengthens the abdomen, hip flexors, and spine
Stimulates kidneys, thyroid, prostate glands, and intestines
Improves digestion and builds mental focus
precautions: Avoid if suffering from asthma, heart disease, or insomnia
Keep knees bent if lower back starts to round or strain
steps: Sit on the floor, legs extended. Bend your knees, lifting your feet off the floor.
Balance on your sit bones and tailbone.
Extend your arms straight forward, parallel to the floor, palms facing in.
Straighten your legs if possible, forming a V-shape with your body.
Keep your chest lifted and spine straight.

ASANAS.name: Salamba Bhujangasana
ASANAS.description: A gentle backbend designed to support the lower back, open the chest, and relieve stress.
benefits: Strengthens the spine and shoulders
Opens the chest and stimulates abdominal organs
Relieves chronic lower back pain and fatigue
precautions: Avoid if experiencing recent abdominal surgeries or severe spinal trauma
steps: Lie on your belly with legs extended straight behind you.
Place your elbows on the floor directly under your shoulders, forearms flat, palms facing down.
Inhale and lift your head and chest off the floor.
Press your forearms firmly into the floor, drawing your shoulders away from your ears.

ASANAS.name: Ananda Balasana
ASANAS.description: A calming supine pose that opens the hips and stretches the lower back, reducing stress and calming the brain.
benefits: Gently stretches the inner groins and back spine
Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and fatigue
Opens tight hips and glutes
precautions: Avoid if suffering from knee or neck injuries
Contraindicated during pregnancy
steps: Lie flat on your back. Exhale, bend your knees, and draw them to your chest.
Hold the outsides of your feet with your hands.
Open your knees slightly wider than your torso, and bring your shins perpendicular to the floor.
Flex your feet and pull down gently on your feet, encouraging knees toward the armpits.

ASANAS.name: Vasisthasana
ASANAS.description: An advanced arm balance that builds wrist, arm, and shoulder strength while engaging obliques and core.
benefits: Strengthens the arms, wrists, shoulders, and legs
Tones and strengthens the obliques and abdominal core
Improves balance, concentration, and coordination
precautions: Avoid if suffering from wrist, elbow, or shoulder injuries
steps: Start in Plank Pose. Roll onto the outer edge of your right foot, stacking your left foot on top of your right.
Place your right hand firmly on the floor directly under your shoulder.
Inhale, reach your left arm up toward the ceiling, creating a straight diagonal line with your body.
Engage your core and lift your hips high, keeping your gaze up at your left hand.

ASANAS.name: Eka Pada Rajakapotasana
ASANAS.description: A deep hip opener that stretches the glutes, psoas, and piriformis, releasing deep-seated tension and stress.
benefits: Deeply opens the hip joints and stretches the piriformis
Stretches the psoas and groin muscles
Releases emotional stress stored in the pelvic region
precautions: Avoid in cases of acute knee or hip injuries
Use support under the hip of the bent leg if it lifts off the floor
steps: Start in Tabletop or Downward-Facing Dog.
Bring your right knee forward and place it behind your right wrist. Angle your right foot toward your left hip.
Slide your left leg straight back behind you, lowering your hips toward the floor.
Inhale, lift your chest, and stretch your spine.
Exhale, fold forward over your right leg, resting your forehead on your hands or the floor.

ASANAS.name: Chakrasana
ASANAS.description: A deep backbend that opens the chest, lungs, and heart, strengthening the arms, shoulders, and legs.
benefits: Stretches the chest, lungs, shoulders, and abdomen
Strengthens the arms, wrists, legs, buttocks, and spine
Stimulates the thyroid and pituitary glands
Boosts energy and helps counteract depression
precautions: Avoid if suffering from high blood pressure, carpal tunnel syndrome, or hernia
Do not practice if experiencing vertigo or headache
steps: Lie on your back, bend your knees, and place your feet flat on the floor close to your buttocks.
Place your hands flat on the floor beside your ears, fingers pointing toward your shoulders.
Inhale, press down through your hands and feet, and lift your body up off the floor, arching your spine.
Straighten your arms and legs as much as possible, letting your head hang down relaxedly.

ASANAS.name: Utthita Parsvakonasana
ASANAS.description: A standing pose that stretches the side body from heel to fingers while building leg strength.
benefits: Strengthens and tones the legs, knees, and ankles
Stretches the groin, spine, waist, chest, and shoulders
Stimulates abdominal organs and increases stamina
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe neck strain; look forward instead of up
Keep the back leg actively engaged to prevent knee strain
steps: Start in Warrior II with your right foot forward.
Lean your torso forward and place your right forearm on your right thigh (or place right hand on floor outside foot).
Reach your left arm up and stretch it diagonally forward over your left ear, palm facing down.
Create a straight line from your left heel all the way through your left fingertips.
Turn your chest open toward the ceiling and look up.

ASANAS.name: Ashta Chandrasana
ASANAS.description: A standing lunge that builds stability and core strength while stretching the hip flexors and chest.
benefits: Strengthens the legs, knees, ankles, and feet
Deeply stretches the psoas and hip flexors of the back leg
Opens the chest and shoulders, improving breathing capacity
precautions: Practice with hands on hips if balancing feels difficult
Avoid in cases of severe knee joint trauma
steps: Start in Downward-Facing Dog. Step your right foot forward between your hands.
Inhale, raise your torso, and sweep your arms overhead, keeping back heel lifted.
Bend your right knee to 90 degrees, directly over the right ankle.
Extend the left leg straight behind you, pressing back through the left heel.
Keep your hips square and tailbone pointing down.

ASANAS.name: Parighasana
ASANAS.description: A lateral stretch that opens the side rib cage and stimulates the lungs and abdominal viscera.
benefits: Stretches the side body, obliques, and intercostal muscles
Stretches the hamstrings and inner groin
Stimulates digestion and respiratory organs, improving breathing
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe knee issues; use a pad under knees
steps: Kneel on the floor. Extend your right leg straight out to the right side, foot flat on the floor.
Inhale and raise your left arm straight up overhead.
Exhale and slide your right hand down your right leg, leaning your torso laterally to the right.
Extend your left arm overhead to the right, opening the left side of your rib cage.

ASANAS.name: Prasarita Padottanasana
ASANAS.description: A wide-legged standing forward fold that stretches the hamstrings and spine while gently inverting the head.
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings, inner thighs, and groin
Decompresses the spine and neck
Calms the brain and helps lower blood pressure
precautions: Avoid if suffering from severe lower back slips or disc herniations
Keep knees slightly bent if hamstrings are stiff
steps: Stand with your feet 3 to 4 feet apart, hands on your hips.
Inhale, lift your chest; exhale, hinge from your hips and fold forward.
Place your hands flat on the floor between your feet, shoulder-width apart.
Lower the crown of your head toward the floor, keeping your neck relaxed.

ASANAS.name: Dolphin Pose
ASANAS.description: A pose similar to Downward Dog but on the forearms, strengthening the shoulders and core in preparation for headstand.
benefits: Strengthens the shoulders, arms, upper back, and core
Stretches the hamstrings, calves, and feet
Helves relieve stress, depression, and headache symptoms
precautions: Avoid if suffering from shoulder or neck injuries
steps: Start on hands and knees. Place your forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders.
Tuck your toes, lift your knees off the mat, and lift your hips high toward the ceiling.
Walk your feet in toward your elbows, keeping your spine straight.
Press your forearms firmly down to keep your head lifted off the floor.

ASANAS.name: Virasana
ASANAS.description: A seated posture that stretches the thighs and ankles, stimulating digestion and serving as a stable pose for meditation.
benefits: Stretches the thighs, knees, and ankles
Improves digestion and relieves gas
Excellent seated posture for pranayama and meditation
precautions: Avoid if suffering from acute knee or ankle injuries
Sit on a block or bolster to relieve joint pressure
steps: Kneel on the floor with your knees touching and feet wider than your hips.
Press the tops of your feet flat on the floor.
Exhale and sit your hips down onto the floor between your feet.
Keep your spine long and rest your hands on your thighs.

PRANAYAMAS.name: Anulom Vilom
benefits: Balances the left (ida) and right (pingala) hemispheres of the brain
Cleanses the nervous system and removes blockages in energy channels (nadis)
Reduces anxiety, stress, and regulates blood pressure
Improves respiratory health and oxygenates blood
precautions: Avoid forcing or holding breath if suffering from heart complications or high blood pressure
steps: Sit comfortably in Sukhasana or Padmasana, spine straight.
Close your right nostril with your right thumb and inhale slowly and deeply through your left nostril.
Close the left nostril with your ring finger, release the thumb, and exhale completely through the right nostril.
Inhale through the right nostril, close it, and exhale through the left nostril.
This completes one round. Continue this alternating pattern smoothly.

PRANAYAMAS.name: Bhramari
benefits: Instantly relieves mental tension, anger, and anxiety
Induces sound sleep, making it highly therapeutic for insomnia
Improves memory and concentration
Soothes the nerves and lowers blood pressure
precautions: Do not practice lying down; always remain seated upright
Do not press the fingers too hard inside the ears
steps: Sit straight with eyes closed.
Place your index fingers on the cartilage of your ears or use Shanmukhi Mudra (closing ears with thumbs, eyes with index fingers, nostrils with middle fingers, and mouth with ring/little fingers).
Inhale deeply through both nostrils.
As you exhale slowly, make a steady, resonant, high-pitched humming sound like a bee ('M-M-M').
Feel the vibrations echoing inside your head and repeat.

PRANAYAMAS.name: Kapalbhati
benefits: Increases metabolic rate, aiding in weight loss and obesity management
Improves function of pancreas, helping to regulate insulin in diabetes
Clears respiratory passages, relieving sinus and asthma congestion
Detoxifies the blood and makes the face radiant (skull-shining)
precautions: Do not practice during pregnancy or menstruation
Strictly avoid if you have high blood pressure, heart diseases, hernia, or gastric ulcers
steps: Sit in a comfortable cross-legged posture with spine straight.
Take a deep breath in through both nostrils.
Exhale forcefully through the nose while contracting the abdominal muscles inward towards the spine.
Inhale passively as the abdomen relaxes naturally (do not force the inhale).
Repeat the active, rapid exhalations at a steady pace (about 60 strokes per minute).

PRANAYAMAS.name: Ujjayi
benefits: Regulates and balances the thyroid gland activities
Calms the nervous system and lowers heart rate
Soothes irritation in the throat and expands lung capacity
Aids in heat generation inside the body, cleansing organs
precautions: Do not tighten the throat excessively; the constriction should be gentle
steps: Sit comfortably with your mouth closed, shoulders relaxed.
Inhale deeply through the nose.
Slightly constrict the back of your throat (the glottis) as you exhale through your nose, creating a soft whispering sound like ocean waves.
Once comfortable, apply the same constriction during inhalation as well.
Maintain a slow, steady, and rhythmic flow of breath.

PRANAYAMAS.name: Sheetali
benefits: Cools down body temperature and reduces internal heat
Reduces acidity, bile (pitta) imbalances, and digestive inflammation
Relieves emotional stress, anger, and frustration
Quenches thirst and helps control blood pressure
precautions: Avoid if you have low blood pressure, asthma, bronchitis, or a heavy cold/cough
Do not practice in highly polluted environments or very cold weather
steps: Sit comfortably, close your eyes, and open your mouth.
Roll your tongue into a tube shape, sticking it out slightly from your lips.
Inhale deeply and slowly through the rolled tongue, feeling a cold sensation in the throat.
Draw the tongue back in, close the mouth, and exhale slowly through your nose.

PRANAYAMAS.name: Nadi Shodhana
benefits: Provides deep purification of all nadis (energetic channels)
Strengthens respiratory system and lung capability
Calms hyperactive thoughts and establishes deep meditation states
Boosts immunity and cellular vitality
precautions: Retention (Kumbhaka) should be avoided by heart patients and those with high blood pressure
Beginners should practice without breath retention first
steps: Sit in an upright, relaxed meditative posture.
Inhale through the left nostril for 4 counts while closing the right nostril.
Hold the breath (Kumbhaka) for 4 to 8 counts (if experienced).
Exhale through the right nostril for 8 counts while closing the left.
Inhale through the right for 4 counts, hold for 4-8 counts, and exhale through the left for 8 counts.

PRANAYAMAS.name: Deep Breathing
benefits: Activates the parasympathetic nervous system (relaxation response)
Maximizes oxygen exchange and strengthens the diaphragm
Lowers cortisol levels and helps control panic attacks
Improves core muscle stability
precautions: Ensure breathing is relaxed; avoid forcing the chest or neck muscles to strain
steps: Sit or lie down comfortably. Place one hand on your chest and the other on your abdomen.
Breathe in slowly through your nose, letting the abdomen expand outward. The chest should remain relatively still.
Exhale slowly through your mouth or nose, letting your abdomen sink back down.
Focus on making the exhalation twice as long as the inhalation.

PRANAYAMAS.name: Bhastrika Pranayama
benefits: Fires up metabolism and increases caloric expenditure
Clears the lungs and bronchial tubes, expanding oxygen intake
Energizes the nervous system and brain, improving alertness
precautions: Absolutely contraindicated for high blood pressure, heart disease, hernia, and ulcers
Do not practice during menstruation or pregnancy
steps: Sit in a comfortable cross-legged position with spine straight.
Make loose fists and place your hands in front of your shoulders.
Inhale vigorously, raising your arms straight up overhead, opening your fists.
Exhale forcefully through your nose, bringing your elbows back down to your ribs, closing your fists.
Perform 15-20 rapid breaths in this manner, then sit silently, observing the energy flow.

PRANAYAMAS.name: Sheetkari Pranayama
benefits: Cools the body, helping manage fever, hot flashes, and heat stress
Soothes the nervous system, reducing anger, anxiety, and blood pressure
Reduces hunger and thirst sensations
precautions: Avoid in cases of severe cold, asthma, or respiratory congestion
Do not practice in cold environments or if teeth are highly sensitive
steps: Sit comfortably with your spine erect.
Keep your lower and upper teeth touching, and open your lips.
Breathe in slowly and deeply through the spaces between your teeth, creating a soft hissing sound.
Close your mouth and exhale slowly through your nose.
Repeat for 10-15 rounds.

PRANAYAMAS.name: Chandra Bhedana
benefits: Activates the Ida Nadi (cooling, parasympathetic pathway)
Reduces heart rate, calms the mind, and manages anxiety and stress
Promotes sound sleep, highly effective for insomnia
precautions: Do not practice if suffering from asthma, cough, cold, or low blood pressure
Avoid during winters or cold weather
steps: Sit in a comfortable posture with your spine straight.
Close your right nostril with your right thumb.
Inhale slowly and deeply through your left nostril.
Close your left nostril with your ring finger, open the right nostril, and exhale slowly through the right nostril.
Always inhale through the left nostril and exhale through the right nostril. Repeat for 10-15 cycles.

PRANAYAMAS.name: Surya Bhedana
benefits: Activates the Pingala Nadi (heating, sympathetic pathway)
Stimulates the digestive fire (Agni) and boosts metabolism
Elevates mood, increases energy, and counteracts lethargy or depression
precautions: Contraindicated for high blood pressure, heart conditions, or high anxiety
Avoid in hot summers
steps: Sit comfortably with your spine straight.
Close your left nostril with your right ring finger.
Inhale slowly and deeply through your right nostril.
Close the right nostril with your thumb, open the left, and exhale slowly through the left nostril.
Always inhale through the right and exhale through the left. Repeat for 10-15 cycles.

PRANAYAMAS.name: Simhasana
benefits: Relieves tension in the face, jaw, throat, and vocal cords
Improves vocal clarity and stimulates the thyroid gland
Stimulates circulation to the throat and facial muscles
precautions: Keep the spine straight; do not strain the jaw excessively
steps: Kneel on the floor, sit back on your heels (Virasana), and place your hands on your knees with fingers spread wide.
Inhale deeply through your nose.
Open your mouth wide, stick your tongue out as far as possible pointing it down toward your chin, and roll your eyes upward.
Exhale forcefully through your mouth, making a deep 'HA' sound from the throat, like a lion's roar.
Perform 3-5 rounds.

DISEASES.name: Heart Disease
DISEASES.description: Conditions affecting the heart structure or function, including coronary artery disease, arrhythmias, and cardiovascular wellness issues. Gentle yoga helps reduce vascular resistance, calms the nervous system, and manages stress.

diet.waterIntake: 2.0 - 2.5 Liters per day (consult physician if experiencing fluid retention)

dailyRoutine: Wake up early (around 5:30 - 6:00 AM) to practice gentle pranayama.
Take a 20-minute slow, mindful walk daily.
Eat light meals; dinner should be finished by 7:30 PM.
Incorporate 10 minutes of deep relaxation (Shavasana) after work.
Maintain a regular sleep schedule, aiming for 7-8 hours of sleep.
homeRemedies: Drink warm water with a pinch of organic garlic paste in the morning.
Consume a teaspoon of Arjun Bark (Arjuna) powder boiled in water/milk once daily.
Chew 3-4 fresh basil (Tulsi) leaves daily on an empty stomach.
precautions: Avoid all inverted poses (e.g., Headstand) and intense backbends.
Do not perform rapid breathing exercises like Kapalbhati or Bhastrika.
Never hold the breath (Kumbhaka) during pranayama.
Perform yoga at a slow, gentle pace without straining.
expectedBenefits: Lower resting heart rate and optimized blood pressure
Reduced stress-induced adrenaline and cortisol release
Improved arterial flexibility and cardiovascular endurance
Restored balance in the autonomic nervous system

DISEASES.name: Diabetes
DISEASES.description: A chronic metabolic condition characterized by high blood sugar levels. Yoga practices compress and massage abdominal organs, stimulating the pancreas to secrete insulin and improving glucose uptake in muscles.

avoid: White bread, white pasta, and white potatoes

dailyRoutine: Begin the morning with 10-15 rounds of Kapalbhati and Anulom Vilom.
Perform twisting and abdominal postures 2 hours after breakfast or on an empty stomach.
Walk for 15 minutes after every major meal.
Monitor blood glucose levels regularly before and after practice.
Sleep by 10:00 PM to regulate stress hormone production.
homeRemedies: Drink bitter gourd (Karela) juice (20-30ml) on an empty stomach every morning.
Soak fenugreek (Methi) seeds overnight in water, drink the water and chew the seeds in the morning.
Consume a mixture of Amla juice and turmeric powder daily.
precautions: Avoid practicing yoga if blood sugar levels are extremely high (>250 mg/dL) or low (<70 mg/dL).
Stay hydrated during sessions.
Avoid holding postures too long if experiencing diabetic neuropathy.
expectedBenefits: Enhanced pancreatic stimulation and improved insulin sensitivity
Reduced fasting and postprandial blood sugar levels
Better management of body weight and cholesterol
Minimized risk of diabetic neuropathies and stress complications

DISEASES.name: High Blood Pressure
DISEASES.description: Hypertension occurs when the force of blood against arterial walls is too high. Mindful breathing and relaxation postures activate the vagus nerve, reducing heart rate and dilating blood vessels.
dailyRoutine: Perform cooling breathwork (Sheetali/Bhramari) immediately after waking.
Dedicate at least 15 minutes to silent meditation or Shavasana.
Incorporate gentle stretches into the day.
Limit sodium in lunch and dinner, focusing on fresh salads.
Maintain a peaceful evening routine, avoiding electronic screens an hour before bed.
homeRemedies: Chew 1-2 cloves of garlic in the morning.
Drink a glass of warm water mixed with half a lemon squeezed and a teaspoon of honey.
Drink watermelon seed powder boiled in water.
precautions: Absolutely avoid Headstands (Sirsasana) and Handstands.
Do not perform rapid, forceful breathing (Kapalbhati, Bhastrika).
Keep the head elevated above the heart in forward bending poses using cushions.
Do not practice holding the breath.
expectedBenefits: Lowered systolic and diastolic blood pressure levels
Reduced vascular tension and increased nitric oxide production
Activation of the parasympathetic (rest-and-digest) system
Reduced risk of strokes and heart attacks

DISEASES.name: Asthma
DISEASES.description: A respiratory condition where airways become narrow, swollen, and produce extra mucus. Deep breathing, chest-opening asanas, and pranayama expand lung capacity, clear bronchial tubes, and calm hyper-reactive airways.
symptoms: Wheezing or whistling sounds during breathing

avoid: Ice creams and curd at night

dailyRoutine: Inhale steam with eucalyptus oil in the morning.
Practice pranayama (especially Ujjayi and Anulom Vilom) in a dust-free, well-ventilated space.
Avoid outdoor exercise during high pollen counts or extreme cold.
Take warm, light meals throughout the day.
Practice deep diaphragmatic breathing when feeling stress rising.
homeRemedies: Boil ginger, black pepper, and Tulsi leaves in water to create an herbal tea. Add honey and drink warm.
Chew a small piece of ginger with a pinch of salt.
Drink warm water with a teaspoon of organic honey before sleep.
precautions: Do not practice during an active asthma attack; use prescribed inhalers.
Keep the throat warm and avoid holding breath if it triggers coughing.
Perform all exercises gently, avoiding overexertion.
expectedBenefits: Expanded vital lung capacity and improved breathing efficiency
Strengthened respiratory muscles (intercostals and diaphragm)
Reduced sensitivity to environmental triggers and stress-induced panic attacks
Clearer airways and easier mucus clearance

DISEASES.name: Obesity
DISEASES.description: Excessive accumulation of body fat that increases the risk of other health issues. Dynamic yoga sequences like Surya Namaskar and metabolic-boosting pranayamas help burn calories, stimulate endocrine glands, and control cravings.
symptoms: Shortness of breath with mild exertion

eat: Warm water with lemon and honey
Super grains like oats and ragi

dailyRoutine: Wake up early and drink 1 glass of lukewarm lemon water.
Dedicate 30-40 minutes to active yoga (e.g., multiple rounds of Surya Namaskar).
Practice Kapalbhati for 5-10 minutes to fire up metabolism.
Avoid sitting continuously for more than 45 minutes; stand or walk.
Have a light salad-based dinner by 7:00 PM.
homeRemedies: Drink warm water with lemon juice and a teaspoon of honey on an empty stomach.
Consume a teaspoon of Triphala powder boiled in water at night before sleep.
Drink warm water boiled with ginger and cumin seeds throughout the day.
precautions: Avoid intense postures if they strain the knees or back; use props.
Progress slowly in Surya Namaskar, starting with fewer rounds.
Avoid sudden jerks, especially in forward bends.
expectedBenefits: Increased daily calorie burn and body fat reduction
Stimulated digestive and metabolic rates
Toned core, back, and limb muscles
Better regulation of appetite and reduced stress-eating

DISEASES.name: Stress
DISEASES.description: A state of mental or emotional strain resulting from adverse circumstances. Restorative yoga, slow pranayama, and mindfulness meditation lower the body's fight-or-flight response and trigger deep relaxation.
dailyRoutine: Begin the day with 10 minutes of silent meditation.
Practice 5 rounds of Bhramari pranayama when feeling overwhelmed.
Take a 10-minute digital break every 2 hours.
Perform a full body scan in Shavasana before going to sleep.
Incorporate hobby or relaxation time in the evening.
homeRemedies: Drink warm milk with a pinch of nutmeg powder before bed.
Massage the soles of the feet with warm sesame oil at night.
Drink chamomile or peppermint herbal tea.
precautions: Do not push yourself into difficult poses that cause frustration.
Focus on the breath rather than perfect alignment.
Keep sessions gentle, centering on relaxation.
expectedBenefits: Reduced levels of stress hormones (cortisol and adrenaline)
Release of muscular tension in neck, shoulders, and back
Improved emotional regulation and mental clarity
Sounder, more restorative sleep cycles

DISEASES.name: Anxiety
DISEASES.description: Characterized by persistent worry, nervousness, or unease. Slow, rhythmic breathing techniques and grounding standing postures help anchor the mind in the present moment, calming hyper-arousal.

eat: Fermented foods (kefir, yogurt) for gut-brain axis

dailyRoutine: Practice deep, diaphragmatic breathing before checking your phone in the morning.
Incorporate grounding standing poses (Tadasana, Tree Pose) to focus the mind.
Take warm, regular meals to soothe the digestive system.
Create a strict sleep hygiene routine: no screens 1 hour before bed.
Practice gratitude journaling or mindfulness for 5 minutes daily.
homeRemedies: Consume a teaspoon of Ashwagandha powder in warm milk at night.
Diffusing lavender or sandalwood essential oils during relaxation.
Sip warm fennel (Saunf) water during the day.
precautions: Avoid breath retention if it triggers feelings of suffocation or panic.
If anxiety arises during a pose, immediately come into Shavasana or Child's Pose.
Focus on soft, lengthening exhalations.
expectedBenefits: Calmed central nervous system response
Lowered heart rate and stabilized respiration
Reduced severity and frequency of panic attacks
Improved ability to witness thoughts without immediate emotional reaction

DISEASES.name: Depression
DISEASES.description: A mood disorder causing persistent feelings of sadness and loss of interest. Dynamic backbends, chest-openers, and energizing breathwork stimulate the nervous system, release endorphins, and lift energy levels.
symptoms: Lack of energy or chronic fatigue

eat: Foods rich in Omega-3 fatty acids

dailyRoutine: Wake up with the sunrise and spend 15 minutes in natural sunlight.
Practice 4-6 rounds of Surya Namaskar to energize the body.
Engage in a social activity or call a loved one daily.
Keep a clean, organized living and practice space.
Go to bed at a consistent hour to regulate circadian rhythms.
homeRemedies: Drink warm milk with a pinch of turmeric and saffron.

avoid: Nightshade vegetables (potatoes, tomatoes, eggplants) if sensitive

dailyRoutine: Perform gentle joint loosening movements (Sukshma Vyayama) in warm water or room.
Practice Anulom Vilom for 10 minutes to reduce systemic inflammation.
Apply warm compresses before starting gentle stretches.
homeRemedies: Drink warm water with turmeric and black pepper.
Apply castor oil packs on painful joints.
precautions: Absolutely avoid strenuous weight-bearing poses during acute inflammatory flares.
Never force joints beyond comfortable range of motion.
expectedBenefits: Reduced systemic inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-a)
Maintained joint range of motion and flexibility
Lowered morning stiffness and pain scores

DISEASES.name: Fibromyalgia
DISEASES.description: Characterized by widespread musculoskeletal pain accompanied by fatigue and sleep issues. Central nervous system desensitization and restorative poses provide relief.
dailyRoutine: Spend 15 minutes in supported Child's Pose (Balasana).
Perform Bhramari pranayama to soothe pain signaling pathways.
Perform very light stretching daily.
homeRemedies: Drink warm chamomile tea before sleep.
Warm oil self-massage (Abhyanga).
precautions: Avoid strenuous postures or long holds; keep sessions restorative.
Use pillows, bolsters, and blankets liberally.
expectedBenefits: Desensitized hyper-reactive pain pathways
Significantly improved sleep quality and deep rest
Reduced daily fatigue and muscle soreness

DISEASES.name: Ankylosing Spondylitis
DISEASES.description: An inflammatory arthritis affecting the spine, leading to fusion. Spinal extension asanas and chest expansion maintain mobility and respiratory capacity.
symptoms: Pain and stiffness in lower back and hips, worse in morning
riskFactors: Age (onset in late adolescence or early adulthood)
dailyRoutine: Perform gentle spinal extensions immediately after morning shower.
Practice deep breathing to maintain thoracic cage flexibility.
Ensure sleeping posture is straight, flat on back with a thin pillow.
homeRemedies: Consume raw turmeric root juice with black pepper.
Warm water bathing with Epsom salts.
precautions: Strictly avoid forward bending poses (e.g. Paschimottanasana) as they promote hunching.
Do not practice during acute pain flare-ups.
expectedBenefits: Maintained spinal extension and flexibility, preventing fusion deformity
Preserved respiratory vital capacity
Relieved chronic back pain

DISEASES.name: Lumbar Spondylosis
DISEASES.description: Degenerative osteoarthritis of the lumbar spine. Decompression poses and core stabilization reduce pain and preserve spinal alignment.
symptoms: Pain worsening after sitting or standing for long
dailyRoutine: Perform gentle bridge poses (Setu Bandhasana) to strengthen glutes.
Rest in Makarasana (Crocodile Pose) for 10 minutes to decompress the lumbar spine.
Avoid lifting heavy weights.
homeRemedies: Apply warm sesame oil mixed with camphor to the lower back.
Drink ginger-honey tea.
precautions: Strictly avoid rounding the lower back in forward folds.
Never twist the spine dynamically or forcefully.
expectedBenefits: Decompressed lumbar discs and nerve roots
Strengthened lower back and core muscles
Reduced lower back stiffness and leg numbness

DISEASES.name: Disc Bulge
DISEASES.description: Outward extension of spinal disc tissue, which can irritate nearby nerves. Back extension poses (Cobra, Sphinx) help draw the disc back into place.
symptoms: Pain in lower back, buttocks, or legs (sciatica)

diet.waterIntake: 3.0 Liters per day (critical for disc hydration)

dailyRoutine: Begin morning with Sphinx pose (Salamba Bhujangasana).
Observe 10 minutes of Viparita Karani with a small pillow under the sacrum.
Avoid bending forward to pick up objects; squat instead.
homeRemedies: Use warm compresses on the lower back.
Massage gently with warm oil.
precautions: Absolutely avoid all forward bends (e.g. Uttanasana, Paschimottanasana).
Do not perform twisting postures.
expectedBenefits: Relieved pressure on nerve roots
Encouraged central retraction of bulged disc
Alleviated acute back pain and sciatica

DISEASES.name: Scoliosis
DISEASES.description: Lateral curvature of the spine. Asymmetrical muscle rebalancing and lateral stretches align the spine and build core symmetry.

eat: Calcium and Vitamin D rich foods

dailyRoutine: Practice lateral stretching (Parighasana) longer on the compressed side.
Focus on standing straight in Tadasana, checking shoulder alignment in a mirror.
Perform gentle core strengthening.
homeRemedies: Warm oil massage on tight back muscles.
Use physical therapy blocks during exercises.
precautions: Do not hold poses that cause sharp pain on one side of the spine.
Always work symmetrically but hold stretches longer on the tight side.
expectedBenefits: Strengthened weak back muscles on convex side; stretched tight muscles on concave side
Improved posture and body alignment symmetry
Reduced chronic muscular back pain

DISEASES.name: Sciatica
DISEASES.description: Pain radiating along the sciatic nerve from the lower back down the legs. Piriformis stretching (Pigeon Pose) decompresses the nerve root.
symptoms: Pain radiating from lower back to leg
dailyRoutine: Massage glutes with warm oil.
Perform gentle Pigeon pose (Eka Pada Rajakapotasana) to release the piriformis muscle.
Walk on level ground, avoiding steep stairs.
homeRemedies: Drink warm milk with garlic and turmeric (Garlic Milk).
Apply warm compress to the lower back and glutes.
precautions: Avoid deep seated forward folds which stretch the sciatic nerve excessively.
Avoid sitting on hard surfaces for long periods.
expectedBenefits: Decompressed sciatic nerve root
Released piriformis muscle tension
Reduced leg shooting pain and restored mobility

DISEASES.name: Frozen Shoulder
DISEASES.description: Adhesive capsulitis causing stiffness and pain in the shoulder joint. Gradual, progressive capsular stretches (Cow Face arms) restore mobility.
symptoms: Dramatically limited range of motion in shoulder
Dull ache in upper arm, worse at night
dailyRoutine: Perform shoulder rolls and arm rotations gently several times a day.
Use a strap in Cow Face Pose (Gomukhasana) to bridge the shoulders without forcing.
Apply a warm compress before starting stretches.
homeRemedies: Massage shoulder with warm sesame oil.
Drink ginger tea.
precautions: Do not force the arm into painful ranges.
Move slowly; let the joint capsule stretch gradually over weeks.
expectedBenefits: Stretched shoulder joint capsule, breaking adhesive fibers
Restored shoulder range of motion
Alleviated night shoulder aches

DISEASES.name: Osteopenia
DISEASES.description: Lower than normal bone density, a precursor to osteoporosis. Weight-bearing standing postures stimulate osteoblast bone-building cells safely.
dailyRoutine: Incorporate 20 minutes of standing weight-bearing asanas daily.
Spend 15 minutes in early morning sunlight for natural Vitamin D.
Perform gentle balance training to prevent falls.
homeRemedies: Eat a spoonful of roasted sesame seeds daily.
Consume dry fig and almond mix.
precautions: Avoid deep twists or sudden movements that could strain vertebrae.
Do not practice advanced inversions like Headstand.
expectedBenefits: Stimulated osteoblast activity, improving bone mass density
Enhanced physical balance, preventing falls
Strengthened surrounding muscular framework

DISEASES.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
DISEASES.description: An autoimmune disease where the immune system attacks multiple organ systems. Parasympathetic activation reduces inflammation and fatigue.
symptoms: Butterfly rash on cheeks and nose
dailyRoutine: Incorporate 15 minutes of gentle breathing (Anulom Vilom) in the morning.
Rest in Shavasana for 20 minutes in the afternoon.
Avoid practicing outdoors in intense sunlight.
homeRemedies: Warm oil self-massage (Abhyanga).
Drink chamomile tea.
precautions: Strictly avoid strenuous physical exertion.
Do not practice during acute inflammatory flare-ups.
expectedBenefits: Attenuated inflammatory response during flares
Alleviated chronic fatigue and joint pain
Enhanced immune regulation

DISEASES.name: Psoriasis
DISEASES.description: A skin disease causing red, itchy scaly patches. Stress reduction down-regulates hyperactive immune signaling and prevents inflammatory flares.
symptoms: Red patches of skin covered with thick, silvery scales
Dry, cracked skin that may bleed
dailyRoutine: Practice cooling pranayamas (Sheetali) to reduce body heat and skin itching.
Apply organic coconut oil to patches before bath.
Perform 15 minutes of mindfulness meditation.
homeRemedies: Apply fresh Aloe vera gel to lesions.
Take oatmeal or Epsom salt baths.
precautions: Do not scratch or rub skin during postures.
Avoid sweating excessively; wipe skin gently with soft towel.
expectedBenefits: Reduced frequency and severity of stress-induced flares
Soother itching and skin inflammation
Normalized immune system activity

DISEASES.name: Chronic Fatigue Syndrome
DISEASES.description: Profound fatigue that can't be explained by any underlying medical condition. Managed by conserving energy via restorative, supportive asanas.
symptoms: Extreme fatigue worsening with physical/mental activity
dailyRoutine: Begin with 5 minutes of alternate nostril breathing.
Practice supported, passive restorative poses with bolsters.
Engage in Yoga Nidra daily for 20 minutes.
homeRemedies: Sip warm ginger-licorice tea.
Take Ashwagandha powder in warm milk.
precautions: Never push yourself to physical exhaustion; practice under active energy pacing.
Avoid hot, exhausting power yoga routines.
expectedBenefits: Conserved metabolic energy and rebuilt reserves
Restored normal sleep architecture
Reduced muscular pain and cognitive fatigue

DISEASES.name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome
DISEASES.description: A functional gastrointestinal disorder affecting the gut-brain axis. Gentle twists and abdominal compression regulate gut motility and relieve cramps.
dailyRoutine: Sit in Vajrasana (Thunderbolt Pose) for 5-10 minutes after every meal to aid digestion.
Practice Pawanmuktasana to expel gas in the morning.
Practice meditation to soothe the gut-brain stress axis.
homeRemedies: Drink warm buttermilk with roasted cumin and mint powder after lunch.
Consume fennel seeds after meals.
precautions: Do not practice abdominal twists on a full stomach.
Avoid strenuous postures if experiencing acute abdominal cramping.
expectedBenefits: Regulated enteric nervous system and gut motility
Reduced abdominal bloating, pain, and gas
Alleviated anxiety and stress-induced bowel spasms

DISEASES.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease
DISEASES.description: Chronic inflammation of the digestive tract (Crohn's or Ulcerative Colitis). Restorative, cooling postures calm mucosal inflammation and support healing.

Observe supported supine poses to relax the abdominal wall.
Minimize stress and practice deep rest.
homeRemedies: Drink fresh pomegranate juice.
Consume licorice root infusion.

expectedBenefits: Soothed gut mucosa via parasympathetic activation
Reduced digestive cramping and diarrhea frequency
Stabilized weight and better nutrition uptake

DISEASES.name: Chronic Constipation
DISEASES.description: Infrequent bowel movements or difficult passage of stools. Abdominal twists, deep squats (Malasana), and morning kriyas stimulate intestinal peristalsis.

riskFactors: Ignoring the urge to pass stool

eat: Clarified butter (Ghee) in warm milk at night

Practice Malasana (Yogi Squat) to encourage pelvic floor relaxation.
Perform Pawanmuktasana to relieve gas and stimulate bowel movement.
homeRemedies: Take a teaspoon of Triphala powder in warm milk or water before sleep.
Eat 4-5 soaked figs in the morning.
precautions: Do not strain excessively during bowel movements.
Practice abdominal compressions on an empty stomach.
expectedBenefits: Stimulated intestinal peristalsis and regular bowel movements
Relaxed pelvic floor muscles for easier elimination
Reduced abdominal bloating and gas

DISEASES.name: GERD
DISEASES.description: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease is chronic acid reflux. Maintaining an upright spine, gentle breathing, and stress management improve esophageal sphincter tone.
symptoms: Regurgitation of food or sour liquid
riskFactors: Eating large meals or eating late at night
dailyRoutine: Sit in Vajrasana for 10 minutes after meals to keep torso upright.
Practice cooling breathwork (Sheetali) to reduce stomach acidity.
Maintain a gap of at least 3 hours between dinner and sleep.
homeRemedies: Chew fennel seeds after meals.
Drink cold milk (in small sips) or coconut water to soothe heartburn.
precautions: Never practice inverted poses (e.g. Halasana, Sirsasana) as they trigger acid reflux.
Avoid forward folds immediately after eating.
expectedBenefits: Strengthened lower esophageal sphincter tone
Reduced stomach acid secretion via stress reduction
Relieved chest burning and regurgitation

DISEASES.name: Endometriosis
DISEASES.description: An often painful disorder where tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside it. Restorative pelvic stretches improve circulation and relieve pain.
symptoms: Pain with bowel movements or urination
riskFactors: Starting period at an early age
dailyRoutine: Practice supported Reclined Bound Angle Pose (Supta Baddha Konasana) for 10 minutes.
Perform alternate nostril breathing to regulate hormonal stress.
Rest deeply during menstruation.
homeRemedies: Apply a warm castor oil pack to the lower abdomen.
Drink ginger tea.
precautions: Avoid active abdominal twists or strong core compression poses during periods.
Do not practice inversions (e.g., Shoulder Stand) during menstruation.
expectedBenefits: Improved pelvic blood circulation and reduced congestion
Alleviated severe menstrual cramps and pelvic pain
Stabilized endocrine and hormonal pathways

DISEASES.name: Menopausal Symptoms
DISEASES.description: Symptoms accompanying the end of menstrual cycles. Cooling pranayamas (Sheetali) reduce hot flashes, while weight-bearing poses preserve bone density.
dailyRoutine: Practice Sheetali pranayama for 10 rounds when hot flashes occur.
Do standing balance poses to maintain coordination and bone health.
Practice Yoga Nidra for 20 minutes to restore sleep quality.
homeRemedies: Consume a teaspoon of Shatavari powder with warm milk at night.
Sip fennel water.
precautions: Avoid high-intensity, heating workouts.
Practice in a well-ventilated, cool room.
expectedBenefits: Reduced frequency and intensity of hot flashes
Restored sleep patterns and reduced night sweats
Stabilized mood and anxiety levels

DISEASES.name: Dysmenorrhea

Dull, constant ache in lower back

Keep legs elevated (Viparita Karani) to relieve lower back pain.
Keep the abdomen warm.

Apply a hot water bag to the lower abdomen.
precautions: Avoid active backbends, inversions, and intense core postures during bleeding.
